mutants.description: min_variance_sdf and min_sdf_std use the raw second-moment matrix E[x x'] where the payoff covariance matrix belongs.
x_star_weights solves Cov(x) b = p (centred moments) instead of E[x x'] b = p.
Sample second moments divide by T - 1 (the unbiased-estimator habit) where the specification demands T.
x_star_weights rescales b so that the SDF has sample mean one (confusing x* with a gross-return normalization).
min_variance_sdf reads its mean argument as the gross riskless rate R_f and imposes E[m] = 1/R_f.
min_variance_sdf and min_sdf_std use a pseudo-inverse and never raise on a singular covariance.
recover_sdf reports the training standard deviation of x* with ddof=1 (sample) where the specification divides by T.
recover_sdf re-estimates x* on the test sample, so its out-of-sample errors are in-sample errors.
recover_sdf estimates the x* weights on train and test pooled (lookahead across the split).
pricing_errors returns per-dollar relative errors E[m x]/p - 1 instead of E[m x] - p in the payoffs' units.
pricing_errors returns p - E[m x] (the opposite sign convention).
recover_sdf returns the hard-coded seed-0 weights instead of estimating them from the training sample.
x_star_weights skips the observation-count and rank checks and relies on np.linalg.solve to fail.
population_x_star weights every state equally (X'X / S) instead of by its probability.
min_sdf_std returns the variance bound (p - v mu)' Sigma^-1 (p - v mu) without the square root.
Input validation never checks for NaN or infinite payoffs, so a NaN sample silently yields NaN weights.
min_variance_sdf returns the intercept a = v instead of v - mu' b, so the SDF v + x' b has the wrong mean.
recover_sdf reports the mean absolute out-of-sample error as out_of_sample_rms.
recover_sdf reports test_share_negative = 0.0 without checking, assuming x* is positive like an SDF.
recover_sdf measures the share of negative x* values on the training sample instead of the test sample.
x_star_weights solves by least squares and silently accepts redundant (linearly dependent) payoffs.
recover_sdf validates train but reads test with np.asarray, so a NaN in the test sample is never rejected.
Input validation rejects NaN with np.isnan but lets +/-inf payoffs and prices through (isfinite was meant).
recover_sdf counts test observations with x* <= 0 (non-positive) as test_share_negative, where the spec says x* < 0.
recover_sdf computes test_share_negative with x* weights refitted on the test sample, not the training weights.
recover_sdf computes test_share_negative with x* weights fitted on train and test pooled (lookahead).
Prices get a length check but no finiteness check, so a NaN or infinite price silently yields NaN weights.
recover_sdf ignores its prices argument and prices every payoff at one dollar, as in the report's currency data.
min_sdf_std skips the finiteness check on its mean argument, so a NaN mean returns NaN instead of raising.
population_x_star reads probs without a finiteness check, so a NaN probability slips past the sign and sum checks.
sdf_values never checks that the weights are finite, so NaN or infinite weights give NaN SDF values silently.
pricing_errors checks the SDF's length but not that its values are finite, so a NaN SDF yields NaN errors.
min_variance_sdf and min_sdf_std drop the covariance rank check and rely on np.linalg.solve to catch singularity.
recover_sdf computes test_share_negative over the training and test rows together, not over the test rows alone.
recover_sdf computes test_share_negative with ridge weights (Lesson 7, lambda = 0.01), not the x* weights.
min_variance_sdf and min_sdf_std reject a NaN mean with math.isnan but accept an infinite mean (isfinite was meant).
Vector arguments (prices, probabilities, weights, SDF values) reject NaN with np.isnan but let +/-inf through.
recover_sdf reports the share of assets with a negative out-of-sample pricing error as test_share_negative.
x_star_weights checks the observation count but leaves redundant payoffs to np.linalg.solve to detect.
recover_sdf divides the count of negative test values of x* by the number of training observations.
population_x_star checks probs with < 0 instead of <= 0, so a state with zero probability is accepted.
x_star_weights rejects T == N observations (off by one: T <= N), although only fewer observations than assets is invalid.
min_variance_sdf rejects a NaN mean with math.isnan but accepts an infinite mean (min_sdf_std is correct).
min_sdf_std forms p - v mu in place on the caller's prices array (np.asarray, no copy), changing its argument.
population_x_star never checks that probs has one entry per state, so a length-1 probs broadcasts silently.
x_star_weights detects redundant payoffs with an absolute threshold |det E_T[x x']| < 1e-12, so payoffs in small units are rejected.
second_moment_matrix reshapes a one-dimensional payoff vector into a single-asset column instead of raising.
min_variance_sdf leaves a debugging print() of the covariance rank in its body, so it writes to stdout.
x_star_weights warns (RuntimeWarning) when the second-moment matrix has condition number above 1e6, then returns the weights.
min_variance_sdf shifts the caller's prices array in place (np.asarray, no copy) while forming p - v mu, so it changes its argument.
sdf_values warns when a value of x' b is negative, reading a negative SDF as a sign of arbitrage.
pricing_errors warns when some SDF value is negative, because a negative SDF must signal arbitrage.
_full_rank rejects redundant payoffs with an absolute singular-value tolerance (1e-10), not a relative one.
population_x_star accepts state probabilities whose sum is within 1e-3 of one, not within 1e-9.
population_x_star demands that the state probabilities sum to exactly one, so float rounding is rejected.
recover_sdf centres the training payoffs before estimating x*, then applies the weights to the raw payoffs.
recover_sdf reports the root of the sum of squared out-of-sample errors, forgetting the division by N.
recover_sdf counts a test x* as negative only below -1e-9, a rounding tolerance the spec does not allow (x* < 0).
x_star_weights rejects full-rank payoffs whose second-moment matrix has condition number above 1e12, a near-singularity guard the spec does not state.
min_variance_sdf and min_sdf_std divide the payoff covariance by T - 1 (the np.cov default) instead of T.
x_star_weights skips the redundant-payoff check when T equals N (square payoffs), so linearly dependent payoffs return garbage weights.
_matrix accepts a payoff sample with zero observations, so second_moment_matrix and pricing_errors divide by zero instead of raising.
min_variance_sdf and min_sdf_std use an absolute singular-value tolerance (1e-10) on the centred payoffs, so a valid sample measured in small units is rejected as singular.
x_star_weights casts the prices to the dtype of the raw payoff array, so integer payoffs truncate fractional prices.
recover_sdf reports train_std with the one-pass formula sqrt(E[m^2] - E[m]^2), which cancels catastrophically when x* has a large mean.
min_sdf_std uses the magnitude of its mean argument, so a negative mean returns the bound for the positive mean.
pricing_errors averages the SDF-weighted payoffs over T - 1 observations instead of T, so every pricing error is inflated by T / (T - 1).
min_sdf_std forgets to centre the prices at the requested mean, so it uses p instead of p - v E[x] as the quadratic form.
population_x_star rescales the state probabilities to sum to one instead of raising ValueError when they do not, so 2 * probs is accepted.
